text: Biosecurity means applying good practices that reduce the risk of disease entering and spreading on a farm; it is easier to apply on a semi-commercial farm with animals kept in premises than in a village with free-ranging animals. To prevent contamination from sick animals: only buy healthy-looking chickens or piglets (bargain-priced animals in poor condition are a bad deal); quarantine newly bought animals for about 2 weeks, since incubation periods run roughly 2 to 15 days, to confirm they stay healthy before mixing them with the rest of the farm; prefer Artificial Insemination over using a boar of unknown health/visit history for mating, since AI avoids direct contact between sow and boar; and de-worm newly purchased cattle 2 days before moving them, since cattle can shed parasite eggs without showing symptoms. To prevent people spreading microbes: limit farm visitors, since other farmers, VAHWs/vets, and anyone returning from market have been exposed to high-microbe environments; always wash hands, since warm, humid hand skin favors microbe survival; have middlemen and outsiders wait at the gate; and have VAHWs/vets change clothes and shoes before and after visiting animals. To prevent vehicles and equipment spreading microbes: clean motorbikes/vehicles returning from Live Bird Markets or egg/chicken delivery runs, and do not allow vehicles onto the farm; clean and disinfect feeders and drinkers bought from a shop before use (since many farmers gather there), and disinfect them regularly on-farm to stop microbes developing in leftover feed. To control pests: manage rodent populations, since they are disease reservoirs; control fly breeding sites (each fly lays about 500 eggs, with only 8 days to a new adult fly) by collecting and drying manure, cleaning spilled feed in pig pens, and regularly cleaning feeders/drinkers; and control mosquitoes by cutting grass around premises, draining puddles, and removing containers of stagnant water. General hygiene — since humid, warm places with organic matter favor pests and microbes — has been shown to reduce animal mortality when villages are cleaned regularly. For water pumped from a pond, cover the storage tank and add chlorine, keeping the water in 20 minutes' contact with the chlorine to properly disinfect it against viruses and bacteria.
